BIG-01.title: The Board Bought Another Company
BIG-01.description: Mike E. walks in mid-project: the Board has acquired a second pharmaceutical company and wants NOVA to manufacture two products instead of one. Scope, benefits case, risk profile, timeline and internal politics all move simultaneously.
BIG-01.pmConcept: Emergency re-planning / scope change at portfolio level
impact: Board Confidence — the only event in the game to move five variables in one beat
possibleChoices: Push back and negotiate a phased approach
accept fully and re-plan WBS+CBS live
accept partially and quietly protect the riskiest workstream
BIG-01.designTag: THE BIG CURVEBALL — the single 'holy crap' moment

EV-R1.title: Supplier Reversal
EV-R1.trigger: Conditional — fires against whichever supplier was NOT chosen in Act 3
EV-R1.description: The unchosen supplier from the Act 3 Procurement Pitch either disappoints badly or turns out to have been the safer bet all along, recontextualising that earlier decision.
EV-R1.pmConcept: Retrospective risk judgement — teaches that a decision can only be evaluated against the information available at the time
possibleChoices: Renegotiate emergency terms with the chosen supplier
fall back to the unchosen supplier at a premium
absorb the impact and adjust the schedule
EV-R1.designTag: AMBIGUITY / REVERSAL — no dominant 'correct' Act 3 choice exists once this fires

EV-R2.title: The Deferred Decision Pays Off
EV-R2.trigger: Conditional — fires if the player deferred or rejected the automated inspection camera change request
EV-R2.description: Budget the player protected by declining an earlier scope addition turns out to be exactly what's needed to absorb BIG-01's re-scoping.
possibleChoices: No choice — a recontextualising narrative beat that shows the consequence of the earlier decision
EV-R2.designTag: AMBIGUITY / REVERSAL — a decision that felt over-cautious in the moment pays off months later

EV-R3.title: The Ally You Didn't Expect
EV-R3.trigger: Conditional — fires if Camille's trust band is Cold/Cool through Act 2–3
EV-R3.description: A stakeholder who spent Acts 1–3 opposing the player (Camille, if under-trusted early) becomes an unexpectedly strong advocate at a critical moment — recontextualising her as an ally rather than an obstacle.
possibleChoices: Accept her support and adjust the plan accordingly
EV-R3.designTag: AMBIGUITY / REVERSAL — an opponent becomes an ally without a single explicit 'trust' choice causing it

EV-R4.title: The 'Bad' Decision That Wasn't
EV-R4.trigger: Conditional — fires if the player chose the cheapest supplier (SteriTech) in Act 3
EV-R4.description: An unexpected external event (a competitor supplier's insolvency) means the player's earlier budget-driven, seemingly risk-laden choice turns out to be the best-positioned option in hindsight.
EV-R4.pmConcept: Judging decisions by process, not just outcome
EV-R4.designTag: AMBIGUITY / REVERSAL — deliberately validates a decision that looked unwise at the time

EV-NP1.title: Isolator Supplier Delay — No Perfect Answer
EV-NP1.description: The isolator supplier confirms a delay. There is no option that protects both budget and schedule.
possibleChoices: Pay to expedite (saves time, costs budget)
absorb the delay (saves budget, costs time) — no third option exists
EV-NP1.designTag: NO PERFECT ANSWER — the trade-off is the design intent, not a puzzle to be solved

EV-NP2.title: Two Products, One Validation Engineer
EV-NP2.description: With two products now in scope, there are not enough validation resources to fully validate both lines on schedule.
possibleChoices: Fully validate Product A on time, delay Product B
split resource thinly across both and accept schedule slip on both
bring in premium contract resource, straining Budget Remaining
EV-NP2.designTag: NO PERFECT ANSWER — every option knowingly under-serves something

EV-01.title: Isolator Supplier Delay (superseded by EV-NP1 in v2)
EV-01.description: Retained from v1 for continuity reference only — see EV-NP1 for the v2 no-perfect-answer version.

EV-02.title: Cleanroom GMP Review Failure
EV-02.description: The cleanroom design fails a Good Manufacturing Practice review.
EV-02.engineNote: Impact should be softened if validation_risk_logged is true (set in ACT2_SCENE04), full severity if false/absent. NEW: if asked_validation_impact is false/absent, apply an EXTRA +5 riskExposure on top of the chosen option's normal effects. NEW: option 3 ('Phase the fix around commissioning') requires asked_validation_mitigation to be true to use its listed effects (scheduleHealth +5, regulatoryReadiness -10, camilleTrust -10) — if false/absent, this option's effects become scheduleHealth -5, regulatoryReadiness -20, camilleTrust -15 instead (the parallel-validation workaround Camille mentioned was never actually planned for, so phasing it in causes more damage).

EV-04.title: Investor Visit Brought Forward
EV-04.description: An investor visit is moved up unexpectedly.
possibleChoices: delay other work to stage the visit

EV-06.title: Electrical Contractor Goes Bankrupt
EV-06.trigger: Conditional (contractor risk flagged in Act 2 unresolved)
possibleChoices: absorb via secondary supplier already on the Risk Register
EV-06.engineNote: Existing severity/softening logic from contractor_risk_logged is unchanged. NEW: if asked_contractor_impact is false/absent, apply an EXTRA +5 riskExposure on top of whatever the chosen EV-06 option's normal effects are (player under-prepared for the true scale). NEW: option 2 ('Absorb via the secondary supplier already on the Risk Register') requires asked_contractor_mitigation to be true to use its listed mild effects (scheduleHealth -3, budgetRemaining -100000) — if that flag is false/absent, this option's effects become scheduleHealth -12, budgetRemaining -350000 instead (the backup was never actually confirmed, so 'absorbing via secondary supplier' turns into an improvised emergency scramble instead).

EV-06-RAID.title: RAID Log — Electrical Contractor
EV-06-RAID.trigger: Follows EV-06 directly whenever it fires — spliced into the MID_WAVE_2 queue right after it, not independently eligibility-gated.
EV-06-RAID.description: The electrical contractor risk has materialised. The player updates the RAID log: owner, immediate response, and whether to escalate.
EV-06-RAID.designTag: RAID mini-artefact — governance follow-up to EV-06, not a scored decision

EV-07.title: Key Automation Engineer Resigns
EV-07.description: An engineer resigns under sustained pressure.

EV-08.title: Extreme Weather Floods the Loading Bay

EV-09.title: Cyberattack Locks the Building Management System

EV-10.title: Finance Freezes Part of the Contingency Budget
possibleChoices: Build the case with the Benefits Register
EV-10.engineNote: Impact should be softened if contingency_risk_logged is true (set in ACT2_SCENE04), full severity if false/absent. NEW: if asked_contingency_impact is false/absent, apply an EXTRA +5 riskExposure on top of the chosen option's normal effects. NEW: option 2 ('Descope a Should requirement') requires asked_contingency_mitigation to be true to use its listed effect (stakeholderGoodwill -5) — if false/absent, this option's effect becomes stakeholderGoodwill -15 instead (without knowing where the slack was, the player descopes something more painful than necessary).

EV-11.title: New MHRA Guidance Note Published
EV-11.description: A new guidance note forces a design review.
possibleChoices: partial review on highest-risk areas only

EV-12.title: Operations Requests Extra Inspection Camera
EV-12.trigger: Conditional (fires after the Change Control scene)
EV-12.description: Priya asks for scope after equipment has already been ordered.

EV-13.title: Supplier Ships Wrong Voltage Equipment
EV-13.description: A critical supplier ships the wrong voltage spec.

EV-14.title: Validation Engineer Poached by a Competitor
EV-14.trigger: Conditional (Team Morale < 50 OR Mike E. Trust Cold/Cool)
EV-14.description: An engineer is poached with commissioning approaching.

EV-E1.description: The original Business Case is missing appendices.
possibleChoices: search shared drive (all lead to the same discovery)

possibleChoices: Log formally in the Risk Register

EV-E3.title: MoSCoW Over-commitment Trap
EV-E3.description: If the player marks everything 'Must', Mike E. notes the budget has just doubled.
possibleChoices: Player self-corrects, or proceeds and carries the budget hit
EV-E3.note: Runtime-triggered reaction inside ACT2_SCENE02's MoSCoW tool (fires if player marks everything Must) — not a standalone scripted scene, so no dedicated dialogue entry.
